rows.text: Under Article 25(2) of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the categories listed in Annex I, Part A always need a notified-body procedure (module B with C, module G or module H). The Part A members are the removable transmission devices and guards, vehicle servicing lifts, portable cartridge-operated fixing machinery, self-evolving safety components, and machinery with self-evolving ML safety systems.

value: Option (a): conformity to type based on internal production control (module C), followed by EU type-examination (module B)
Conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)
Conformity based on unit verification (module G)
rows.text: For machinery in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer must apply one of the Article 25(2) procedures: option (a), EU type-examination (module B) followed by internal production control (module C); full quality assurance (module H); or unit verification (module G).

rows.value: Annex I, Part A, point 5: safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour.
rows.text: A safety component with self-evolving behaviour falls under the category of safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour, listed in Annex I, Part A, point 5.

rows.value: Interlocking movable guards must be used instead of fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged, as set out in Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation.
rows.text: Under Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards rather than fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged.

value: Risks related to moving parts
rows.text: Under Annex III, point 1.3.7 of the Regulation addresses risks related to moving parts.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification, under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, is subject to the manufacturer's obligations in Article 10, where the modification affects only the safety of machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery.
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification is subject to the manufacturer's obligations in Article 10, provided the modification affects only the safety of machinery or a related product forming part of an assembly of machinery. That person must also ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility.

rows.text: Under the Regulation (EU) on machinery, machinery or related products must be accompanied by the instructions for use and the information in Article 10(7) and Annex III (Art. 10(7), Art. 13(4)), by the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 10(8), Art. 15(2)), and by the required documents (Art. 13(2)); where size or nature prevents it, a document accompanying the machinery is required (Art. 10(5)). These obligations apply from 2027-01-20, the Regulation's general application date.

The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for at least 10 years, counted from when the machinery or product is placed on the market or put into service (Machinery Regulation, Art. 10(3) and Art. 12(2)).
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 generally applies from 20 January 2027 (fact 0). Several specific Articles apply earlier, from dates such as 19 July 2023, 20 July 2024, 20 January 2024 and 20 October 2026.
Yes. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed only from 20 January 2027 (Corrigendum, points 5 and 6), so conforming machinery can still be placed on the market on 16 January 2027.

rows.value: INAIL carries out the first periodic verification, within 45 days of receiving the complete request.
rows.text: For the equipment in Annex VII, the first periodic verification is carried out by INAIL (DM 2011, art. 2, c. 1), within 45 days of receiving the complete request (INAIL guide). INAIL may delegate it to a qualified body designated by the employer.
The employer must keep at least the results of the checks under art. 71, comma 8 for the last three years (art. 71, comma 9, D.Lgs. 81/2008).

rows.text: The Regulation's new corruption-protection requirement is in Annex III, point 1.1.9, which requires that software and data critical for compliance, and hardware components transmitting signals or data relevant to access to such software, be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption.

The DEMAG overhead travelling crane (IGEA device 8) must be verified once a year, under DLGS Allegato VII, riga 15. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

The Effer truck-mounted crane (IGEA device 7, 790 kg, built 2017, mining site) must be verified every year, per the Annex VII row 12 sector rule for mobile lifting equipment above 200 kg. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

rows.value: ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale), for the periodic verifications subsequent to the first.
rows.text: Under DM2011 art. 2 c. 1, the subsequent periodic verifications of the Annex VII equipment are carried out by the ASL, while the first is carried out by INAIL.

The first periodic verification must be carried out within 45 days of receipt of the complete request, as set by Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 and the INAIL guide. The sixty-day figure attributed to the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 is not supported by the available facts.
No. Under the UR e-Series manual (p. 220), the UR5e may only be put into service once integrated into a final complete machine, since it is partly completed machinery.
The nanoScan3 must be tested at least once a year, per the regular tests, detection-capability test and principal-function thorough check in the nanoScan3 manual (pp. 50–51).
The verifier (aggiudicatario) must give IGEA at least 15 days' notice of the planning of the checks (igea-equipment, p. 5).

The IGEA overhead travelling crane at position 13 must be verified every two years, under the Annex VII (D.Lgs. 81/2008) row for fixed lifting equipment in the quarrying sector, built within the last 10 years. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

IGEA device 13 must be verified every P2Y on 2026-11-14: GRU A PONTE SCORREVOLE is lifting equipment of type fisso (mapping of the rule); capacity 5000 kg is above 200 kg; sector estrattivo: named in the row; built in 2017: not more than 10 years before 2026-11-14; Annex VII row for type fisso, sector use, age new. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.
